channel.title: Nicotine Science and Policy
channel.description: Daily digest of views, debates and discussions on nicotine science, policy, regulation and advocacy.

item.title: Kuwait Tightens Tobacco and Nicotine Rules, Bans Under-21 Sales and Extends Public Smoking Restrictions to Vapes and Heated Tobacco
item.description: Kuwait’s new nicotine rules place vapes and heated tobacco firmly inside the smoking-control framework. That may simplify enforcement, but it also risks flattening important differences between combustible and non-combustible products. Protecting young people and limiting public exposure are legitimate goals, yet regulation should still preserve a clear pathway for adult smokers to move away from cigarettes. Policy becomes stronger when control is matched with a credible understanding of relative risk. (Published on August 18, 2026by2firsts.com)

item.title: Brazil's Vaping Coverage Has Become a Misinformation Assembly Line
item.description: Brazil’s vaping debate shows how quickly misinformation can become a policy machine. Repeated claims about risk, youth use and regulation shape public understanding long before evidence is given proper context. That matters because smokers may be left believing that legal cigarettes are no more dangerous than smoke-free alternatives. Public health communication should correct confusion, not manufacture it. (Published on August 19, 2026byworldvapersalliance.com)

item.title: EU tobacco consultation exposes growing divide
item.description: The EU tobacco consultation has exposed a deeper disagreement about the purpose of nicotine policy. One side treats all nicotine use as the problem; the other asks how to reduce the far greater harms caused by smoking. That divide matters because regulation built around abstinence alone can leave adult smokers with fewer credible alternatives to cigarettes. Europe needs a framework that recognises risk differences, protects young people and allows harm reduction to contribute to lower smoking rates. (Published on August 19, 2026bybrusselssignal.eu)

item.title: Britain’s Latest Public Health Threat Is Cheesecake, According to the Government
item.description: Britain’s public health debate is drifting into absurdity. Treating everyday choices as threats to be managed from above risks replacing guidance with control and responsibility with restriction. The same instinct appears in tobacco and nicotine policy: regulate the behaviour, narrow the options, and call it protection. Public health works better with trust, proportion and evidence than with a constant search for the next thing to ban. (Published on August 19, 2026bythe360mag.com)

item.title: The Tobacco Control Antis Have a Problem
item.description: Australia’s tobacco debate has reached the point where defending the status quo is no longer enough. High excise, illicit cigarettes, restricted vape access and organised crime are now part of the same policy landscape. Stronger enforcement may be necessary, but it cannot answer the economic incentives that keep the black market attractive. A serious nicotine strategy would make safer legal options easier to access than illegal cigarettes. (Published on August 19, 2026bysubstack.com)
